mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (below 0.5%) signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 0.5%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 5.5%, it signals a weakening labor market that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 60% of instances when UNRATE > 5.5%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, which triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS are below their 3-month moving averages, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a supply contraction regime (INDPRO below 105), manufacturing output slowdowns reduce corporate profitability and lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of instances when INDPRO < 105, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A strong labor market, indicated by rising employment (PAYEMS), boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 60% of instances when PAYEMS is above its 3-month moving average, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year CPI inflation exceeds 3.0%, it signals persistent inflation that may trigger monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL (yoy) > 3.0%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of slowing GDP growth (GDPC1) and declining housing starts (HOUST) indicates a weakening economic expansion, which results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of instances when both GDPC1 and HOUST are below their 6-month moving averages, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening regime (FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and CPIAUCSL > 3.0% yoy), rising interest rates and persistent inflation lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and CPIAUCSL (yoy) > 3.0%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
